claims.title: The expression language
notes: PRODUCT FINDING — the Arrow→RecordSet seam decodes a DATE column to epoch-milliseconds while the engine's Value::Date expects i32 days, so serde refuses the whole ingest of any dated result (`invalid value: integer 1735862400000, expected i32`). annual-orders.csv is the first dated source the seam has met; this chapter drives it with order_date withheld and says so in the margin.

SEAM FINDING — the barcode lowering feeds the bound rectangle's STORED geometry to the page-local insertPath wire, so on this page (stored offset -540,0) every module landed one page width off, on the pasteboard; the page translated the fresh modules back by the measured offset in one batch.

claims.title: Four symbologies, one order book
notes: SEAM FINDING — the four symbols (and the re-drawn expression specimens) landed one page width off (stored offset -540,0); translated back by the measured offset in one batch before classification.
lowerAll re-drew the expression page's bound symbols onto this page (584 stray path modules) — removed; a re-lower always draws afresh onto the active page rather than replacing in place.

UPC-A — upc: no modules — the likely cause is the CSV type sniffer reading the leading-zero UPC column numerically (072034010010 → 72034010010), an 11-digit value no UPC-A encoder accepts; the missing policy drew nothing rather than a fake symbol.

claims.title: A native table, governed
notes: lowerAll re-drew the six bound symbols during the table pass — 1118 stray path modules removed from the active page.

the lowered table paints past its frame (a native table ignores the frame's bottom bound), so the page trimmed it to one header and eight records via deleteTableRow — an ordinary table edit, stated on the page.
